title: Uniqueness, analyticity and mixing for Gibbs point processes via spectral gaps
summary: A Gibbs point process models particles interacting in the continuum through a potential. Among the most classical examples is the hard-sphere model, where given an activity parameter $λ$, a radius $r$, and a bounded set $Λ\subset \mathbb{R}^d$ one samples a Poisson process of intensity $λ$ in $Λ$ conditioned on the points forming the centers of an $r$-sphere packing. We prove uniqueness of infinite-volume Gibbs measure, analyticity of the pressure, and various notions of spatial and temporal mixing for activities up to what we define as the spectral threshold $λ_{spec}$ of the potential.
